title: The waiting mark ends three ways so it can never become a permanent lie
action: Give the waiting mark from ah-1 three independent ways to end, all live at once (per D2). ONE: the `UserPromptSubmit` hook clears it the moment the human sends anything. That hook is hooks/prompt_context.rs — it already runs on every human message and composes the phase/gate reminder in `build_prompt_reminder`. This is the reliable layer, because it fires on a real human action instead of on the agent remembering. It must be BEST-EFFORT: a clear that fails must never fail the hook or break the turn, matching the try-once, lock-losing discipline the other opportunistic hooks already use. TWO: an explicit clear the agent calls when it acts on the answer — the sibling of ah-1's setter. Clearing a mark that does not exist is a no-op, not an error. THREE: stale expiry, and this is the one with a trap. Per D4 it reuses the DUAL-CONDITION rule cells/claims.rs already applies: a mark expires only when its age is past the threshold AND the owning session's heartbeat is stale. Expiry alone must NEVER clear a mark — a human who simply took twenty minutes to answer must not have the wait silently erased while their session is plainly alive. Read the claim sweep before writing this: it excludes the caller's own session first, then re-verifies both conditions. Write the test that pins the trap: age past the threshold, heartbeat FRESH, mark SURVIVES.

truths: The human sending a message clears a live mark through the UserPromptSubmit hook
A failing clear inside the hook never fails the hook or the turn
The agent can clear a mark explicitly, and clearing a mark that does not exist is a no-op rather than an error
A mark whose age is past the threshold but whose owning session heartbeat is FRESH survives
A mark whose age is past the threshold and whose owning session heartbeat is stale expires

prompt_context.rs:2409 run_survives_a_failing_clear_without_failing_the_hook_or_skipping_its_output, #[cfg(unix)], chmods `.bee/` to 0o555 after pre-creating locks/, cache/, logs/. The injection is genuinely targeted, not decorative: fsutil.rs:139-145 write_json_atomic builds its tmp via tmp_path_for(file) — the target file's OWN directory, i.e. `.bee/` — so the clear's write to .bee/state.json cannot create its tmp, while mark_injected's target (prompt_context.rs:860 = .bee/cache/inject-cache.json) sits in a still-writable subdir. Non-vacuity is asserted, not assumed, three ways: (a) the mark is asserted STILL LIVE after run() (:2454) — had the injection silently done nothing, the clear would have succeeded and this assert fails; (b) outcome is Done, not Delegate; (c) .bee/cache/inject-cache.json must exist, and that file is created only by mark_injected inside execute() at :305 — so the early-return paths at run():136/142/158, which never reach the clear, cannot satisfy it. Ran green: `test ...run_survives_a_failing_clear_without_failing_the_hook_or_skipping_its_output ... ok`.

Noted for the record, not a failure. The final assert (:2475) only checks that .bee/logs/hooks.jsonl contains "prompt-context", which is HOOK_NAME for every log_crash in the file — the heartbeat_block crash at :286 would also match under the same read-only `.bee/`. So that one line does not uniquely prove the CLEAR's failure was logged. It is redundant belt-and-braces: the must_have truth (a failing clear never fails the hook or the turn) is carried by the Done outcome, the completed inject-cache write, and the still-live mark, all three unambiguous.

No change to what the UserPromptSubmit hook emits: b7b422f9 has zero '-' lines and adds nothing outside `mod tests`; stdout composition at prompt_context.rs:300-325 is untouched. No new store: no new file, no new path — the mark still lives in .bee/state.json and the workflow record. No expiry on age alone: record.rs is not touched by this commit; the conjunction at record.rs:532 stands.
